reality_delta: Only a plan exists. No implementation, diff, test, or runtime evidence has changed yet. The 'changed_reality' items are prior failure observations, not proof the fixes are in place.
main_concern: The audit-mode tester/reviewer path risks becoming a soft bypass around the developer-readiness gate. If Loom records any downstream role-run artifact after exhaustion, future scripts or humans may read it as 'the pipeline progressed,' even if it does not literally mark E2E passed. The plan is still a narrative until concrete invariants and tests exist.
top_risks: Audit-mode diagnostic handoff becomes normalized as an acceptable next step, eroding the strict-gate culture the user wants.
Session-chain tracking adds a new data model without a proven mapping to actual Hook session ids, which could recreate false missing_session_id alarms.
Timeout and probe-selection fixes are underspecified; shorter outer timeouts could hide slow root causes instead of diagnosing them.
missing_evidence: A concrete spec for how selected Hook session ids are persisted and matched in role-run artifacts.
The audit-mode artifact schema with explicit, testable guarantees that it can never emit a pass signal.
Proposed timeout bounds and a mapping from child-probe exit codes/timeouts to diagnostic evidence.
minimum_fix: Implement the fixes behind verifiable tests: repeated repair sessions record the correct session id; developer exhaustion launches audit-mode reviewer only and never sets E2E passed; package Prism timeout produces a clear child-probe diagnostic; relation probe selects a domain activity title. Re-review on test output, not on the plan.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The plan keeps saying 'do not weaken gates' and 'keep completion blocked.' Those must become hard-coded assertions in tests or config, not just phrases in a document, to prevent the next cycle from mistaking a well-written plan for a working system.

user_intent_alignment: Directionally aligned: the fixes target runtime mechanisms and Loom strictness rather than producing more TRPG demo content. However, the user wants a better workflow machine, so a plan alone is insufficient; the next deliverable must be working code with evidence.
